subject: history
title: Edward VI and Mary I
welcome_lead: From Protestant prayer books to Smithfield fires: religious whiplash 1547-58.
meta_desc: A-Level history adventure on the mid-Tudor crisis, Edwardian Reformation and Marian reaction.
final_note: You have walked between Cranmer's Prayer Book and Pole's restoration.

concepts.def: Henry VIII's Protestant son (1547-53), under whom England became formally Protestant.
Cranmer's English liturgy; first edition 1549, more Protestant revision 1552.
1553 Protestant doctrinal statement that did not become enforced before Edward's death.
Reluctant Protestant claimant proclaimed queen on 10 July 1553, displaced after nine days by Mary.
Mary I's reign (1553-58) reversing Reformation legislation and reuniting England with Rome in 1554.
1555-58 burning of about 280 Protestants including Cranmer (March 1556) for heresy.

walkthroughs.body_html: Edward's regency, under Somerset until 1549 then Northumberland, dismantled Catholic structures. The 1547 Chantries Act abolished masses for the dead. The 1549 Act of Uniformity imposed Cranmer's Prayer Book, prompting the Western Rebellion. The 1552 Prayer Book denied real presence. The Forty-Two Articles (June 1553) defined Protestant doctrine just weeks before Edward's death.

Mary I rapidly repealed Edwardian legislation. Statute of Repeal in 1553 restored the 1547 religious settlement; the second Statute of Repeal in January 1555 undid the Henrician break with Rome. Cardinal Reginald Pole reconciled the realm in November 1554. Heresy laws revived; burnings began in February 1555 with John Rogers, totalling around 280 executions by 1558.

A.G. Dickens portrayed Marian restoration as anachronistic. Eamon Duffy's Stripping of the Altars (1992) and Fires of Faith (2009) argue Marian church was vigorous and successful, with substantial parish reform under Pole. The 1557 loss of Calais and Mary's death in November 1558 cut short a potentially enduring restoration, leaving Elizabeth to settle religious affairs.

mcqs.q: Approximately how many Protestants were burned under Mary?
Why was the Spanish Armada defeated in 1588?
options: Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
Drake defeated the Armada single-handedly in a great sea battle.
Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
A combination of English tactics and fireships, poor Spanish planning, and the 'Protestant wind' storms that wrecked the fleet on the return.

mcqs.q: Why did Henry VIII break with Rome?
options: William of Orange was Charles II's son and inherited the throne.
Because he wanted England to become Protestant.
Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
Primarily for an annulment from Catherine of Aragon, but also to seize Church wealth and assert royal supremacy — not for Protestant theological reasons.
